title: Germany – Railway bridge construction work – Ern. KRBW Wiesbaden Biebrich Str. 3505, Km 44,020. VE 1 KIB/OB
description: Das geplante Bauvorhaben befindet sich im Stadtgebiet der hessischen Landeshauptstadt Wiesbaden in der Gemarkung Biebrich. Der nächstgelegene Bahnhof Wiesbaden-Ost liegt in ca. 700 m südlicher Richtung an der Strecke 3603. Das Kreuzungsbauwerk liegt zwischen dem Salzbach und der Autobahn A 671 auf der elektrifizierten Strecke 3505 im Richtungsgleis Wiesbaden Hbf–Wiesbaden Biebrich bei km 44,020. Das Bauwerk überführt die elektrifizierten Strecken 3603 Frankfurt Hbf–Wiesbaden Hbf in km 38,4 und 3528 Mainz Kaiserbrücke Ost-Wiesbaden Hbf in km 6,9. Die von der Erneuerung betroffenen Strecke ist die Strecke 3505 Richtungsgleis. Die Erneuerung des Kreuzungsbauwerks sieht eine eingleisige Fachwerkbrücke. Diese wird als Einfeldbauwerk mit 100m Stützweite jeweils hinter den bestehenden denkmalgeschützten Widerlagern des vorhandenen Bauwerks gegründet. Der Kreuzungswinkels beträgt 19,1 gon. Die Widerlager werden ist in Ortbeton mit Tiefgründung hergestellt. Die Ausbildung des Stahlfachwerkkonstruktion erfolgt gemäß Ril 804.9010, Kap.2. Der Überbau ist mit insgesamt 4 Kalottenlagern längsbeweglich und querfest auf den Widerlagern gelagert. Die querfeste Lagerreihe ist auf der Innenseite des Gleisbogens angeordnet. Längskräfte sowie Längsverformungen der Brücke werden über einen Steuerstab (System Meyer-Wunstorf) auf beide Widerlager verteilt. Die Gleislage wird um ca. 1,70m in der Mitte der neuen Brücke erhöht, somit ergibt sich einen neuen Oberbauabschnitt von ca. 620m. Im Anschluss zur neuen geplanten Fachwerkbrücke Richtung südwest befindet sich eine denkmalgeschützte Gewölbebrücke. Diese muss aufgrund der neuen Erdlasten (wegen Dammerhöhung) gesichert werden. Das Gewölbe wird mit einem Stahlbetondeckel überbaut und somit dauerhaft entlastet. Das Deckelbauwerk über dem Gewölbe wird auf einer Länge von ca. 58,35 m von km 44,0+87 bis km 44,1+45 (Richtungsgleis Strecke 3505) als Rahmentragwerk errichtet, welches auf 2 überschnittenen Bohrpfahlwänden aufgelagert ist und Horizontallasten planmäßig über Schrägpfähle abträgt. Direkt im Anschluss an das Deckelbauwerk muss ab km 44,145 der neue Bahnkörper abgefangen werden. Von km 44,145 bis km 44,183 ist eine neue Fahrwegplatte mit Tiefgründung gem. Ril 836 geplant. Da sich im Anschluss an die Fahrwegplatte zwischen km 44,183 bis km 44,278 rechts des Richtungsgleises Strecke 3505 immer noch der Anrampungsbereich befindet und das Gleis gleichzeitig in Teilbereichen bis zu 1,15 m nach rechts abrückt, wird hier eine Stützkonstruktion auf ca. 100 m Länge notwendig. An dieser Stelle ist eine Spundwand mit Rückverankerung und Kopfbalken aus Stahlbeton geplant. Am nördlichen linken Dammfuß des neuen Richtungsgleises Strecke 3505 im Anschluss an die Fachwerkbrücke werden in etwa zwischen km 43,890 und km 43,920 sowie zwischen km 43,943 und km 43,973 Fertigteil-Winkelstützwände auf einer Länge von insgesamt 51 m zum Schutz der Hauptkabeltresse notwendig. Die Winkelstützwände sind außerhalb von Eisenbahnverkehrslasten auf einer Magerbetonschicht und darunter liegender Frostschutzschicht zu gründen

title: Denmark – Safety consultancy services – Managed Detection and Response (MDR)
description: Med henblik på at beskytte Statens IT (Ordregiver) mod aktuelle og fremtidige cybertrusler anvender Ordregiver en række sikkerhedsteknologier, herunder en Extended Detection and Response (XDR)-platform. XDR-platformen understøtter indsamling, korrelation og analyse af sikkerhedsrelaterede hændelser på tværs af Ordregivers it-miljø med henblik på at beskytte systemer, tjenester og data samt sikre dataenes fortrolighed, integritet og tilgængelighed. Henset hertil udbyder Ordregiver en kontrakt, hvis formål er at understøtte og styrke Ordregivers egen operative it-sikkerhed gennem levering af en Managed Detection and Response (MDR)-tjeneste fra et Security Operations Center (SOC). MDR-tjenesten skal anvende og supplere Ordregivers XDR-platform med døgnbemandet overvågning, analyse, detektion, validering, eskalering og håndtering af sikkerhedshændelser. Tjenesten skal leveres 24 timer i døgnet, 365 dage om året, og bidrage til hurtig identifikation, vurdering og håndtering af cybertrusler og sikkerhedshændelser. Tjenesteydelserne udgør et væsentligt element i Ordregivers fortsatte modnings- og udviklingsproces på cybersikkerhedsområdet med fokus på teknologi, processer, kompetencer og samarbejde på tværs af interne og eksterne interessenter. Med udbuddet ønsker Ordregiver adgang til en professionel MDR-tjeneste, der kan imødekomme Ordregivers høje krav til kvalitet, robusthed og effektivitet, samt en leverandør, der løbende kan indgå i dialog med Ordregiver om udviklingen inden for cybersikkerhed, herunder trusselsbilledet, teknologiske muligheder, automatisering, kompetenceudvikling og løbende forbedringer af sikkerhedsniveauet. Leverandøren skal gennemføre en teknisk, organisatorisk og processuel Transition Ind, der sikrer, at de løbende MDR-ydelser kan leveres fra overgang til driftsfasen. Ordregiver gør opmærksom på, at Ordregiver har indgået kontrakt med to (2) leverandører til varetagelse af Ordregivers eksisterende XDR-platform, som leverandøren skal samarbejde med i forbindelse med Transition Ind. Som led heri skal leverandøren etablere og konfigurere de nødvendige integrationer mellem Ordregivers XDR-platform og øvrige relevante sikkerhedskilder samt leverandørens værktøjer og platforme, der anvendes til kontraktens opfyldelse. Leverandøren skal levere Løbende MDR-ydelser; herunder kontinuerlig overvågning, analyse, korrelation, validering og detektion af alarmer og sikkerhedshændelser. Leverandøren skal foretage triagering og kvalificering af alarmer med henblik på at identificere reelle sikkerhedshændelser samt sikre rettidig eskalering og advisering i overensstemmelse med aftalte processer og serviceniveauer. Disse løbende MDR-ydelser omfatter herunder: • Kontinuerlig SOC-overvågning af sikkerhedsrelaterede hændelser og alarmer. • Analyse, korrelation og kvalificering af hændelser på tværs af relevante datakilder. • Identifikation, detektion og validering af sikkerhedshændelser. • Udarbejdelse, implementering og løbende optimering af detektionsregler, use cases og analysemodeller. • Anvendelse af relevant Threat Intelligence til understøttelse af detektions- og analysearbejdet. • Løbende vurdering af trusselsbilledet og dets relevans for Ordregivers miljø. • Proaktiv identifikation af potentielle sikkerhedshændelser og sikkerhedsrisici, herunder gennem Threat Hunting-aktiviteter. • Eskalering, advisering og rapportering af sikkerhedshændelser i henhold til aftalte processer og serviceniveauer. • Vedligeholdelse af eksisterende integrationer samt etablering af nye integrationer efter behov. • Optimering og videreudvikling af Ordregivers XDR-platform og øvrige sikkerhedsløsninger. • Rådgivning vedrørende udvikling og modning af Ordregivers sikkerhedsorganisation, sikkerhedsprocesser og governance. • Gennemførelse af målrettede Threat Hunting-forløb og analyser af mistænkelige aktiviteter. • Incident Response-bistand ved sikkerhedshændelser efter rekvisition fra Ordregiver, herunder analyse, afgrænsning, håndtering, afhjælpning og genopretning. • Bistand ved større sikkerhedshændelser, cyberkriser og koordination med relevante interessenter. • Sikkerhedsfaglig rådgivning og strategisk sparring om udviklingen inden for cybersikkerhed. Kontrakten omfatter desuden tværgående ydelser, herunder dokumentation, rapportering, governance, kvalitetssikring og informationssikkerhed, der leveres gennem hele kontraktperioden. Endvidere omfatter kontrakten forpligtelser ved kontraktophør (Transition Ud), der skal sikre en kontrolleret, sikker og dokumenteret overdragelse af viden, data, processer, integrationer og øvrige kontraktrelaterede leverancer til Ordregiver eller en efterfølgende leverandør.

title: USS Patrick Gallagher (DDG-127) Custom Galley Table and Chair Covers
description: PART I: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & GENERAL PROCUREMENT DESCRIPTION This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) under solicitation number N6278626Q0007. The resulting contract will be awarded as a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) purchase order. Procurement Overview: This requirement is to procure custom-fitted, heavy-duty marine-grade Naugahyde vinyl table and seating covers for the Wardroom, Chief Petty Officer (CPO) Mess, and Crews Mess of the newly built guided-missile destroyer USS Patrick Gallagher (DDG-127). All dimensions listed in this solicitation and the associated Attachment 1 are physical estimates based on prior vessel configurations. Physical dimensions must be verified by the contractor via an on-site measuring and templating visit at the location of the ship, which is not limited to the shipyard in Bath, Maine, or in Norfolk, Virginia, post-award, before final production begins. Attachments: The following document is incorporated into and made a part of this solicitation: Attachment 1: Technical Specifications (DDG-127 Galley Covers) � Outlines the estimated material fabric standards, stitching colors, graphic etching sublimation sizes, and detailed configurations for all 15 technical CLINs. PART II: SCHEDULE OF SUPPLIES / SERVICES (CLIN STRUCTURE) Bidders shall format their pricing based upon the CLINs being requested. All quotes must be firm-fixed-price and encompass all material manufacturing, customization, graphics, shipping, on-site measurements, and final travel fittings. CLIN Description CLIN 0001 Wardroom Table Cover IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each CLIN 0002 Wardroom Utility Table Cover IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each CLIN 0003 CPO Mess Table Cover (Medium) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each CLIN 0004 CPO Mess Table Cover (Large) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 3 Each CLIN 0005 Crews Mess Table Cover (Standard A) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 11 Each CLIN 0006 Crews Mess Table Cover (Compact) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 2 Each CLIN 0007 Crews Mess Table Cover (Standard B) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 5 Each CLIN 0008 Crews Mess Table Cover (Bench A) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each CLIN 0009 Crews Mess Table Cover (Bench B) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each 0010 Wardroom Seat Cover (Style 1 - Standard) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 19 Each CLIN 0011 Wardroom Seat Cover (Style 2 - CO) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each CLIN 0012 Wardroom Seat Cover (Style 3 - XO) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each CLIN 0013 CPO Seat Cover (Rank Insignia & Crest) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 20 Each CLIN 0014 Mess Deck Swivel Seat Cover (with 2" Foam) IAW Attachment 1 Specs 66 Each CLIN 0015 CPO CMC Seat Cover IAW Attachment 1 Specs 1 Each CLIN 0016 Travel & Measuring Lot: Travel/Lodging to Bath, ME (On-site measurements) and Naval Station Norfolk, VA (Final check-fit and delivery execution) 1 Lot TOTAL BID PRICE (CLINs 0001 - 0016): $__________ PART III: STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) / REQUIREMENTS 1.0 General Requirements The Contractor shall fabricate, customize, package, deliver, and perform on-site fitting checks for table covers, seat slipcovers, and bench cushions for the Wardroom, Chief Petty Officer (CPO) Mess, and Crews Mess of the USS Patrick Gallagher (DDG-127) in accordance with Attachment 1: Technical Specifications. 2.0 Location of Performance & Shipboard Delivery Due to shipboard requirements, performance shall be executed in two sequential geographic phases: On-Site Measurements & Templating (Post-Award): The Contractor shall travel to the location of the ship to conduct physical measurements and construct precise templates of all messing tables and seating. The locations of the ship will be at Bath, ME or Norfolk, VA depending on the operational timeline. No fabrication shall occur until physical measurements are completed and final graphic designs are approved. Final Delivery & Check-Fitting: Final delivery, installation, and fit-testing shall be performed on-board the ship at Naval Station Norfolk, Virginia. The Contractor shall perform any necessary on-site tailoring or snug-fit adjustments. 3.0 Summary Technical Specifications (Governed by Attachment 1) Fabric Composition: Marine-grade, water-impermeable Naugahyde vinyl (Colors per Attachment 1). Fire Safety Standards: All fabrics must meet OPNAVINST 5100.19F afloat safety standards, NFPA 701, and FAR 25.853 flame-retardant standards. Flammability laboratory test sheets must be submitted for review. Border Text & Stitching: All table covers must have rounded corners with a sewn overhang drop. Drops must feature screen-printed or etching sublimated block letters governed by Attachment 1. Table Graphics: High-resolution full-color etching sublimation of the official Ship�s Crest centered on the tops. Screen prints, physical embroidery, stickers, or adhesive-backed decals are strictly prohibited on tabletop surfaces. title: EEA/CCE/TC/26/010 - Topic Centre on Climate Risk and Resilience: Knowledge Development
description: To drive progress towards a climate resilience Europe, the EEA will continue providing essential data, information and policy-relevant insights that inform the design and implementation of adaptation measures, risk management strategies and societal preparedness efforts. A key priority is to track and assess progress on EU's climate resilience. Knowledge exchange will support EU Member States in preparing national climate risk assessments and adaptation policies. The EEA will also play a role in the implementation of potential outcomes for the foreseen European Integrated Framework for Climate Resilience. With a focus on resilience indicators, sectoral progress and broader economic and societal resilience, the EEA aims to develop relevant and actionable knowledge products for Europe. The focus of this new Topic Centre will be predominantly on the knowledge and networking services. However, tasks under these services will also cover some data services and will build on work conducted under the Topic Centre on Climate and Resilience: Reporting, Tools and Online Knowledge support. As such, collaboration is expected between the two Topic Centres.

title: Romania – Washing and dry-cleaning services – „Prestari servicii de leasing, intretinere si igienizare pentru imbracamintea de protectie”
description: Implementarea Serviciului de leasing, intretinere si igienizare pentru echipamentele de protectie este necesara pentru asigurarea unui proces operational standardizat, sustenabil si conform cerintelor de igiena si siguranta aplicabile domeniului de activitate. Achizitia acestui serviciu reprezinta o solutie oportuna, avand in vedere limitarile si dezavantajele generate de modelul actual bazat pe achizitia directa a articolelor. Serviciul permite externalizarea integrala a proceselor de igienizare, intretinere, reparatii si inlocuire, reducand semnificativ sarcina administrativa si eliminand costurile asociate gestionarii interne. Furnizorul asigura trasabilitate digitala avansata (RFID / coduri de bare), schimburi regulate, stoc tampon, distributie controlata si conformitate permanenta cu standardele SSM. De asemenea, serviciul contribuie la reducerea consumului de resurse si la alinierea la obiectivele de sustenabilitate ale companiei. Achizitia acestui serviciu ofera oportunitatea optimizarii fluxurilor operationale, reducerii riscurilor si asigurarii unei imagini profesionale constante a personalului. Prestatorul trebuie sa asigure un serviciu complet, integrat, care include urmatoarele componente principale: • Leasing pentru echipamentele de protectie – punerea la dispozitia angajatilor a articolelor de imbracaminte de protectie conform specificatiilor tehnice din Caietul de Sarcini, cu personalizare nominala (logo, etichetare RFID/cod de bare), sesiuni de proba individuale pentru stabilirea masurilor corecte si transfer de proprietate la finalul contractului; • Igienizare si intretinere – flux complet industrial: colectare articole murdare din toate locatiile beneficiarului, triere, spalare cu dezinfectare conform standardelor profesionale, uscare controlata, calcare/calandrare, finisare, inspectie calitativa, impachetare, sortare pe purtatori si livrare in cusete nominale. Zonele curate si murdare trebuie gestionate separat; • Reparatii si inlocuiri – detectarea articolelor neconforme (rupte, descusute, deteriorate), reparatii fara costuri suplimentare, inlocuirea articolelor cu uzura normala in 1-2 cicluri de rotatie; • Instalare vestiare si cusete – furnizarea, livrarea si instalarea celor necesare desfasurarii serviciului, inclusiv cusete nominale individuale cu sistem de inchidere securizat si vestiar colector pentru articole murdare, separat fizic de zona curata; • Platforma informatica digitala – sistem de trasabilitate cu vizibilitate in timp real: status fiecare articol (curat/murdar/in proces), numar cicluri de spalare, istoric reparatii si inlocuiri, alocari pe utilizatori, rapoarte lunare, export CSV/XLSX, disponibilitate minima 99%; • Instruire utilizatori – sesiune initiala obligatorie pentru toti angajatii. Cantitati estimate ale acordului cadru/contract subsecvent: Conform Anexa 11, document atasat la prezenta documentatie. Frecventa contractelor subsecvente ce vor fi atribuite este de 1/an. Valoarea estimata a celui mai mare contract subsecvent este: 13,789,001.63 lei, fara TVA. Entitatea contact va raspunde in mod clar tuturor solicitarilor de clarificari sau informatiilor suplimentare in a 11 a zi, inainte de termenul limita stabilit pentru depunerea solicitarilor de participare, conform prev art.172 al (2) si 173 al (1) din Legea 99/2016 actualizata. Numar zile pana la care se pot solicita clarificari inainte de data limita de depunere a solicitarilor de participare/ofertelor: 20 zile. Entit contr va raspunde doar la solicitarile de clarificari adresate de operatorii economici pana la termenul-limita stabilit, conform art. 29 alin. (3) din HG 394/2016. Eventualele solicitari de clarificari la documentatia de atribuire vor fi adresate la adresa de mail: l.matea@reteleelectrice.ro Raspunsul consolidat la eventualele solicitari de clarificari la documentatia de atribuire se va publica in Seap.

Om het eiland hiervoor geschikt te maken zijn in hoofdzaak de volgende werkzaamheden nodig: aanpassen van kades en oevers, maken van een inkassing in de oever van de Oude Maas, aanbrengen van paalfunderingen t.b.v. steunpunten, aanbrengen van een fundatie en balk voor een skidbaan en het verder inrichting van het werfterrein. title: FY27 United Kingdom Wage and Benefit Study Re-Acquisition
description: SOLICITATON NOTICE: The 700th Contracting Squadron (700 CONS) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) purchase order on a sole source basis to Croner Group Limited (Cage Code: U1AA3); (Unique Entity ID: YL5XL93NM3Y8). This intended contract will cover services in support of the FY27 United Kingdom Wage and Benefit Study Re-Acquisition. The anticipated award date is 30 November 2026. This requirement is to be awarded as a multiple-year follow-on contract inclusive of one (1) 12-month base period with four (4) 12-month option periods in accordance with (IAW) Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 52.217-9. This requirement also includes the Option to Extend Services not to exceed (NTE) 6-months IAW RFO 52.217-8. This intended contract follows the guidance stated in the Department of Defense Manual (DoDM) 1416.08 which mandates compensation for local national personnel supporting U.S. Forces components in the United Kingdom to be based on salary and benefit data analysis. Consistency in the methodology and data source used for these studies is necessary to maintain year-to-year comparability and ensure changes in salary and benefits can be accurately measured. Croner Group Limited is the incumbent contractor under Contract No. FA561322P0008 and currently provides the salary and benefit data used to support this requirement. Croner utilizes established internal systems, methodologies, and historical data to provide consistent employment, wage, and benefit information to the Government. The current contract expires on 31 December 2026, and this follow-on acquisition is intended to ensure continuity of these services. In accordance with RFO 6.103-1, Croner Group Limited is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the Government�s requirement without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delays. Award to another source would require the Government and a new contractor to establish a new methodology and data baseline for the wage and benefit studies. This would disrupt year-to-year comparability with historical data and require additional time and resources to establish replacement processes. Additionally, transitioning to another source would create a risk of incompatibility between historical and newly collected salary and benefit data, which could negatively affect the Government�s ability to consistently evaluate changes in compensation. Croner�s established processes and historical data provide the continuity necessary to support the Government�s compensation analysis. Accordingly, the Government intends to solicit and award to Croner Group Limited as the only responsible source capable of meeting this requirement. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. However interested parties may submit a capability statement upon the referenced deadline within the attached solicitation (FA561327Q0001) demonstrating their ability to perform the requirement described herein. Upon receipt of any such notifications, the Contracting Officer will determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement or proceed with sole source action. Responses received will be reviewed, however; a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, the 700 CONS will proceed with the sole source award to Croner Group Limited. See attached solicitation (COMBO-SOLICITATION FA561327Q0001)

title: FY27 United Kingdom Wage and Benefit Study Re-Acquisition
description: SOLICITATON NOTICE: The 700th Contracting Squadron (700 CONS) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) purchase order on a sole source basis to Croner Group Limited (Cage Code: U1AA3); (Unique Entity ID: YL5XL93NM3Y8). This intended contract will cover services in support of the FY27 United Kingdom Wage and Benefit Study Re-Acquisition. The anticipated award date is 30 November 2026. This requirement is to be awarded as a multiple-year follow-on contract inclusive of one (1) 12-month base period with four (4) 12-month option periods in accordance with (IAW) Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 52.217-9. This requirement also includes the Option to Extend Services not to exceed (NTE) 6-months IAW RFO 52.217-8. This intended contract follows the guidance stated in the Department of Defense Manual (DoDM) 1416.08 which mandates compensation for local national personnel supporting U.S. Forces components in the United Kingdom to be based on salary and benefit data analysis. Consistency in the methodology and data source used for these studies is necessary to maintain year-to-year comparability and ensure changes in salary and benefits can be accurately measured. Croner Group Limited is the incumbent contractor under Contract No. FA561322P0008 and currently provides the salary and benefit data used to support this requirement. Croner utilizes established internal systems, methodologies, and historical data to provide consistent employment, wage, and benefit information to the Government. The current contract expires on 31 December 2026, and this follow-on acquisition is intended to ensure continuity of these services. In accordance with RFO 6.103-1, Croner Group Limited is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the Government�s requirement without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delays. Award to another source would require the Government and a new contractor to establish a new methodology and data baseline for the wage and benefit studies. This would disrupt year-to-year comparability with historical data and require additional time and resources to establish replacement processes. Additionally, transitioning to another source would create a risk of incompatibility between historical and newly collected salary and benefit data, which could negatively affect the Government�s ability to consistently evaluate changes in compensation. Croner�s established processes and historical data provide the continuity necessary to support the Government�s compensation analysis. Accordingly, the Government intends to solicit and award to Croner Group Limited as the only responsible source capable of meeting this requirement. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. However interested parties may submit a capability statement upon the referenced deadline within the attached solicitation (FA561327Q0001) demonstrating their ability to perform the requirement described herein. Upon receipt of any such notifications, the Contracting Officer will determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement or proceed with sole source action. Responses received will be reviewed, however; a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, the 700 CONS will proceed with the sole source award to Croner Group Limited. See attached solicitation (COMBO-SOLICITATION FA561327Q0001)

title: Board of Management Secure Online Portal
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) intends to enter into a contract with a single contractor for the provision of a secure online portal for its Corporate Secretariat with access for a maximum of forty (40) active users. The Portal must be a browser- and app-based software as a service (SAAS) used to upload, store, view, search for, print, share, download, edit and annotate documents. The Portal will be used by the CRA, its Board of Management, and other external committees (as required), and will be administered by the CRA’s Corporate Secretariat. The Portal will be a central repository for Board materials, documents and communication, thereby providing a secure and efficient environment to access materials and prepare for Board meetings. For additional information, consult Annex A, Statement of Work of the bid solicitation document. This requirement also includes options to extend the term of the contract by up to six additional one-year periods under the same terms and conditions and to add, remove or modify products or services. The estimated period of any resulting contract will be for one year from the date of contract award. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. Questions must be directed in writing to via email: Marie-Claude.Lepage@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. title: Urinalysis Collection - Timmins
description: This bid solicitation cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 21470-29-5128698B dated May 11, 2026 that closed June 8, 2026 at 14:00 EDT. A debriefing or feedback session will be provided upon request to bidders/offerors/suppliers who bid on the previous solicitation. Urinalysis sample collection for offenders This requirement is for: The Correctional Service of Canada, Timmins, Ontario Trade agreement: This procurement is not subject to any trade agreement. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the statement of work for this requirement. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to provide Urinalysis Collection Services for both male and female offenders in Timmins and the surrounding geographical area. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: Consistent with the Mission Statement and Strategic Objectives of the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC), the contractor must provide a Urinalysis Collection Program for the Timmins area and extending to the surrounding rural areas. 1.2 Tasks: 1.2.1 The Contractor must: 1. Upon referral, collect urine samples from federally released male and female offenders. 2. Provide a collector that must be of the same gender as the offender providing the sample. 3. Accurately label, store and package samples to prevent contamination or tampering. 4. Record necessary information, including time of collection, collector identification, and complete other required documentation. 5. Explain the urinalysis process clearly to offenders, maintaining a calm and respectful demeanor. 6. Handle potentially sensitive or uncomfortable situations with discretion and empathy. 7. Ensure the integrity of the sample by placing the required seals on the container, obtain signatures on the container, and prepare the container for shipment to the specified laboratory for testing. 8. Ship the samples with a bill of lading to the approved laboratory for testing. 9. Collect samples in compliance with Section 66(1) of the CCRA regulations, and CD 566/566-11. The contractor must provide protective gloves to the collectors. 10. Present the offender with form 1064-1 (Community Notification to Provide a Urine Sample) prior to the initial test or at the beginning of a new frequency of urine collection if CSC requests one, obtain the offender’s signature, complete the Chain of Custody Form 1065 for every sample collected and distribute copies of the form as directed. 11. Complete the urinalysis log sheets monthly, or provide a detailed invoice, or both, and forward them to the respective office responsible for the supervision of the offender. 12. Attend court hearings, meetings with auditors, or meet with CSC managers as requested. 13. For all cases assessed by CSC to meet the tandem supervision policy, the contractor must provide a collector and an additional member of its staff or a person approved by the project authority who must accompany the collector whenever a urine sample is collected in the offender's private residence or in an isolated community location (CD 715). CSC will brief both the collector and the additional member of the contractor's staff or approved person on safety concerns. 14. Immediately notify the CSC supervising parole office if the collector notes that an offender refuses or is unable to provide a sample, or displays any suspicious behaviour, or both. If this occurs outside the contractor’s established working schedule, the contractor must follow the National Monitoring Centre protocol. 1.2.2 Collection Schedule: 1. Normally, the contractor must perform collections during regular working hours, Monday to Friday, between 0700 hours and 1800 hours. 2. CSC may request that the contractor collect urine samples, from time to time, on weekends and after normal working hours. 3. CSC may request that the contractor collect urine samples on an emergency basis. The contractor must respond within 3 to 4 hours of being notified of an emergency requirement. 4. The contractor must respond within 24 hours’ notice for any non urgent requests to schedule collection. 1.2.3 Continuity of Services 1. The collector must provide 24 hours’ notice for cancellation of collections. The contractor must provide this notice to the Office Urinalysis Coordinator. 2. The contractor must provide a back-up for urinalysis collection, in case of illness, vacation, leave, or the inability to provide urinalysis collection services for at least 5 days. The contractor must obtain the Departmental Representative’s or Project Authority’s prior approval before the back-up performs any work. The back-up must also complete the CSC Urinalysis Collectors Orientation Program (at the contractor’s expense) before the back-up begins providing any urine collection services. 1.2.4 Support the Contractor CSC will: 1. Ensure that the contractor is provided with all necessary documentation including Regulations, Directives, and Guidelines for compliance to be maintained. 2. Provide procedural instructions for the surveillance, procurement and shipment of samples. 3. Refer offenders for urinalysis testing. 4. Establish procedures for shipment of samples to the CSC specified laboratory for testing. 5. Facilitate the process of securing Reliability Status security clearance for the contractor and/or subcontractor providing the services. 6. Provide the required paperwork, sample containers, courier bags, courier bills of lading, a cooler to store the collection samples and an appropriate security storage container for paperwork and referrals. 7. Provide a complete CSC Urinalysis Collectors Orientation Program prior to the collector commencing any urine collection services. The orientation includes safety procedures related to reporting negative offender behaviour to the CSC supervising parole office, and the National Monitoring Centre protocol. 1.2.5 Cancellations The contractor must not charge CSC when CSC provides at least 24 hours of notice of cancellation of collections. The Parole Officer Supervisor, CCC Manager, or Office Urinalysis Coordinator will provide this notice. When CSC provides less than 24 hours notice of cancellation of collection, the contractor may charge one-half the collection rate. The Parole Officer Supervisor, CCC Manager or Office Urinalysis Coordinator will provide the cancellation notice by Telephone notification or telephone message to the contractor. 1.2.6 No Show Fee If an offender does not show up for collection of a urine sample, the contractor may claim a maximum of 3 hours at the firm hourly rate. This fee shall only apply if the contractor scheduled a single collection. It will not apply when the contractor scheduled multiple collections for the same time period and at least one offender shows up. 1.3 Location of work: The Contractor must perform the work in the City of Timmins, its 5 wards, and the surrounding area including Parole Offices, Reporting Centre, Community-Based Residential Facility (CBRF), community correctional Centres (CCC), designated locations as approved and arranged by the Case Management Team and at offenders’ private residences as requested. 1.3.1 Travel CSC will reimburse the contractor’s travel expenses incurred for the collection of urine samples only for collections outside the City of Timmins Area and it’s 5 wards. 1.3.2 Travel time The contractor may claim travel time for the time the contractor’s collectors require to travel from the City of Timmins and it’s 5 Wards to the designated urinalysis col

title: Ireland – Repair and maintenance services of electrical and mechanical building installations – Provision of Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Control, and Automation (MEICA) Support Services for Licensed Landfills in County Donegal.
description: Donegal County Council invites tenders from competent service providers for the provision of comprehensive Mechanical, Electrical, Instrumentation, Control, and Automation (MEICA) support services across six closed landfill facilities in County Donegal. The successful contractor will be required to deliver routine preventative maintenance, emergency fault diagnostics, 24/7/365 rapid response call-out interventions, and component updates on specialised environmental infrastructure. The scope of works includes troubleshooting industrial automation platforms, tuning SCADA/telemetry networks, field instrumentation calibrations (such as inline electromagnetic flow meters), electrofusion/butt welding on chemical pipework, and localised pump upkeep. Major capital replacement materials will typically be supplied by the Council for installation by the contractor. The contract will be established for an initial fixed term of one (1) year, with the unilateral option for Donegal County Council to extend the agreement for an additional period of up to one (1) year subject to performance and budget authorisation. Bids will be evaluated via a two-stage Open Procedure based on Pass/Fail suitability followed by Lowest Cost.

title: Labor Market Transparency & Fraud Detection Tools - RFI/Industry Day
description: 1. Purpose The U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 10, Market Research, to identify commercially available platforms that can support DOL�s efforts to improve labor market transparency, workforce identity verification, employment compliance, and detection of potential fraud and unlawful labor practices. The information received will assist the Government in understanding industry capabilities, refining requirements, assessing risks, and developing an appropriate acquisition strategy consistent with applicable procurement laws and regulations. This RFI is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quote, or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any supplies or services. 2. Project Overview DOL is exploring commercially available digital workforce identity and compliance platforms that can provide secure, verifiable data to improve labor market transparency and identify indicators of potential fraud. Specifically, DOL seeks solutions offering trusted identity verification and work authorization status for workers, portable digital credentials (e.g., certifications, training and licensing records) that workers can share with employers or regulators, and electronic records of key compliance activities (such as wage payments, safety training completion, housing and transportation inspections, and worksite assignments) to support employers in meeting labor standards. The ideal platform will generate audit-ready logs and reports of employment and compliance data, use data analytics to flag potential fraud, document inconsistencies, or unlawful labor practices, and support greater transparency in the workforce (for example, by confirming that workers are deployed as authorized and that required conditions are being upheld). Importantly, any solution must incorporate privacy and security by design, obtain appropriate consent for personal data use, and complement existing legal employment verification and worker protection processes. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 513210 (Software Publishers). 3. Requested Information DOL requests that interested parties address the following areas: A. Company Information Company name, address, and point of contact Business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) Relevant NAICS codes Primary point of contact Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Applicable contract vehicles that the solution is available (if any) B. Relevant Experience Description of experience providing labor market transparency and fraud detection tools Experience working with federal agencies Examples of similar projects/contracts completed within the last 5 � 7 years C. Technical Capabilities and Anticipated Approach Capabilities related to providing labor market transparency and fraud detection tools How does your solution differentiate itself from alternative options on the market? Does your solution include artificial intelligence? If yes, to what extent? What reporting, analytics, or data insights will your platform provide, and how often? What is the estimated timeline to fully deploy this solution? What kind of initial and ongoing training or support do you provide to clients? How is cybersecurity addressed for the solution? D. Cost Considerations Please provide a high-level, Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) for your solution. Describe the pricing model, such as a subscription, user-based, usage-based, etc. What are the major cost drivers? Is the proposed solution available through an existing Government-wide acquisition contract? 4. Industry Day DOL intends to host an Industry Day to provide interested vendors with an opportunity to demonstrate their relevant capabilities. Tentative Date: September 24 - 25, 2026 Location: Virtual Format: Presentation and demo via MS Teams DOL may request vendors to demonstrate one or more of the following conditions within their solution: A. Worker Identity How a worker establishes and maintains a trusted digital identity and how an authorized employer or Government user verifies the identity. B. Digital Credentials How a worker receives, maintains, and securely shares a digital certification or safety-training credential and how an authorized party validates the credential. C. Compliance How employment and compliance information, such as wage payments, training completion, worksite assignments, or inspection records, is collected and maintained. D. Fraud Detection How the platform identifies an inconsistency or anomalous pattern across multiple records and generates an alert or risk indicator for further human review. E. Investigation and Audit How an authorized DOL user examines supporting information, identifies the source of the underlying data, and generates an audit-ready report. F. Privacy and Security How the platform manages consent, user access, data sharing, privacy controls, security controls, and audit logs. Vendors should be prepared to identify which capabilities demonstrated are currently commercially available, which are configurable, and which would require customization or new development. DOL requests that respondents address the following questions during Industry Day, as applicable: What data sources are required to operate the solution effectively? What sources can the solution access or integrate with? What information (if any) should be collected directly from workers, employers, Government agencies, or other sources? What are the primary privacy risks associated with a digital workforce identity platform? How can DOL minimize collection and retention of unnecessary personal information? How should human review be incorporated into fraud detection and compliance workflows? What steps are taken to minimize false positives? What interoperability standards should DOL consider? What integration challenges should DOL anticipate? What is a reasonable implementation timeline for a solution of this nature? What level of Government involvement is typically required during implementation? What is the general period of performance on contracts for your solution? What performance metrics should DOL consider when evaluating such a solution? Pick one fraud/compliance alert in the demo and walk us from the alert all the way back to every underlying data element. Which data came from the worker, employer, government, third party, or the platform itself? Which data are verified versus self-reported? Show us an employer trying to game the system What does the investigator actually receive? Can workers/employers record events without connectivity? How are timestamps and integrity preserved? How are conflicting offline records reconciled later? Can DOL export its data, schemas, audit logs and reports in usable nonproprietary formats? What happens to credentials issued to workers? What happens if the vendor fails, is acquired, or DOL changes providers? What are the five failure modes and which party controls each one: vendor, DOL, another federal agency, state, employer, or worker Which visa programs do they leverage / work with? Please expressly address credential expiration Who owns the data? Can the data be repurposed and, if so, under what conditions? 5. Industry Day Submission Interested vendors shall submit their responses by 10:00am (EST) on 9/17/2026 to Contracting Officer (CO) Broderick Morris at Morris.Broderick@dol.gov. Registration is required to attend the industry day. Attendees shall provide the following information with their email to Broderick Morris: Subject Line: RSVP Industry Day � DOL Labor Market Transparency & Fraud Detection Tools Company Name and Business Size (Include applicable socio-economic status) Name of Attendee(s) Attendee(s) Contact Information (Email and Phone N

description: 1. Description of Requirement The 166th Airlift Wing, Delaware Air National Guard, intends to issue a firm-fixed-price task order on a noncompetitive basis to Veteran Equipment Sales LLC (VES), the manufacturer of the Government-furnished equipment (GFE), for the installation, integration, testing, startup, training, and commissioning services of a GFE VES heated semi down-draft aircraft paint booth system with attached mixing room at the Nose Dock Repair Facility. Additionally, as an option line item, funding dependent, the contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, transportation, tools, equipment, materials, supplies, factory-certified personnel, and incidental services necessary to install, integrate, test, startup, train Government personnel, and commission a Government-furnished VES NIOSH-Compliant Personnel Air Shower. The Government-furnished equipment includes: VES Personnel Air Shower: VES Part Number 965-100-001, National Stock Number 4460-01-698-7874 VES Paint Booth System: VES Part Number PB-100-000, National Stock Number 4940-01-707-5264 The Government is currently constructing a new fuel cell to house the equipment. Consequently, the contractor's installation schedule may be dependent upon the progress and completion of the Government's construction activities. 2. Manufacturer Certification and Warranty Requirements VES has advised the Government that third-party installers may perform installation only if the installers have been factory-trained and certified by VES prior to performing installation work. Each certified individual must possess written certification signed by the President of VES confirming the individual's qualification. VES further requires that, regardless of the installer's certification status, a VES factory-trained and certified field engineer must be present on site to supervise installation and perform startup and training in order to maintain the manufacturer's warranty. Because the requirement involves installation, integration, testing, startup, training, and commissioning of VES-manufactured equipment, the Government must ensure that the contractor can satisfy all applicable VES factory-certification, supervision, startup, training, and warranty requirements. 3. Intent and Capability Submission Instructions Based on the information presently available to the Government, VES is the intended source for this requirement. However, the Government is seeking information from other responsible sources to determine whether there are qualified sources capable of performing the complete requirement while satisfying the manufacturer's requirements. Interested sources are invited to submit information demonstrating their capability to perform the complete requirement. Responses from sources other than VES shall provide sufficient information for the Contracting Officer to determine whether the respondent can satisfy all requirements. At a minimum, respondents should identify: Their relationship or authorization status with VES Their ability to provide VES factory-trained and certified personnel to perform the installation Documentation demonstrating applicable VES factory certification signed by the President of VES Their ability to provide or coordinate the required VES factory-trained and certified field engineer to supervise installation and perform startup and training Their ability to install, integrate, test, start up, training Goverment personnel, and commission the Government-furnished VES equipment Their ability to satisfy all applicable VES manufacturer requirements necessary to maintain the equipment and equipment warranty Responses should clearly demonstrate the ability to perform the entire scope of work, including all required labor, supervision, transportation, tools, equipment, materials, supplies, factory-certified personnel, and incidental services. 4. Submission Deadline and Point of Contact Responses must be recieved no later than 17 September 2026, at 10:00 a.m. EST. Please submit all responses via email to Ms. Katesha Tolson at katesha.tolson.1@us.af.mil 5. Notice Disclaimer This notice is not a request for quotations or a solicitation. The Government will consider infromation received from responsible sources in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy.

description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT This notice is issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) section 5.201 to notify the public of a proposed contract action. The North American Identification Classification System (NAICS) code is 811210 Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance . The SBA size standard is f $34 million in average annual receipt. The proposed contract action is for a modification to an exisiting contract under which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 6.302(c)(1). The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C.253(c)(1) as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1 entitled �3304(a)(1) sole source specifications, which reads in part, �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements.� The U.S Agency of Global Marketing (USAGM) intends to modify contract no. 951700-21-F-0193 awarded to Tower Facilities Management, LLC (Tower FM) for replacement, repair and maintnenance of our Uninterupted Power Supply (UPS) systems manufactured by General Electric, due to an urgent requirement for UPS replancement and repair. The mission critical requirement is necessary to provide back-up power to the building should an unforeseeable power outage occur. If power to the building fails, there would be operational delays due to system disruptions. The Voice of America (VOA) and United States Agency for Global Media (USAGM) have an immediate and most urgent requirement to procure certified General Electric (GE) manufacture technicians to provide maitnenace services to replace 2 Module Inv/Rectifier, 1 module Booster and 1 Bridge Can Bus Cable necessary for the repair of UPS#2 located int the UPS Room Garage Level 330 Independence Avenue, Washington, DC, 20237. This UPS repair will provide back-up power for our critical infrastructure to the building needed to support the agncey's mission. Tower FM is the only contractor known to immediate respond to this emergency and perform repairs on the General Electric (GE) Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS) systems supporting this requirement. Tower FM maintains proprietary rights and access necessary to service GE UPS equipment, and its technicians possess specialized factory training that uniquely qualifies them to diagnose, repair, maintain, and provide technical recommendations for these systems with in 48 hours. Due to its exclusive authorization and specialized expertise, Tower FM is capable of ensuring repairs are performed in accordance with GE manufacturer's specifications and operational requirements. Utilizing Tower FM minimizes operational risk, supports system reliability, and helps ensure continued performance of critical power infrastructure. No other known source can provide the same level of authorized support, proprietary knowledge, and factory-trained technical services required for these GE UPS systems within the required timeframe. title: Request For Information (RFI) Web Based Respirator Medical Questionnaire & Evaluation Tool
description: Web-Based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool I. Introductory This is a Request for Information. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Request for Information is to obtain details, capabilities and clarification from potential suppliers and knowledge and information on potential vendor interest for project planning purposes. II. Project Description Background Federal Occupational Health (FOH), a component of the Program Support Center (PSC) within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), provides occupational health services to more than 360 federal agencies and supports approximately 1.8 million federal employees throughout the United States, U.S. Territories, and internationally. As part of these services, FOH administers respirator medical evaluation and clearance services to assist customer agencies in complying with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) Respiratory Protection Standard (29 CFR 1910.134). FOH currently utilizes a web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool to support respirator medical evaluation and clearance activities. As the current contractual arrangement approaches its conclusion and the Government's cybersecurity, identity management, and operational requirements continue to evolve, FOH is conducting market research to identify vendors capable of providing, configuring, or developing a web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool that satisfies the Government's functional, clinical, operational, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and identity management requirements. Information obtained through this Request for Information (RFI) will assist the Government in determining available commercial capabilities, implementation approaches, technical maturity, and acquisition strategies for this requirement. Purpose and Objectives The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to conduct market research to identify qualified vendors capable of providing, configuring, or developing a secure, web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool that satisfies the Government's requirements. The Government is seeking information regarding commercially available products, configurable commercial platforms, or custom-developed solutions capable of supporting OSHA-compliant respirator medical questionnaire and evaluation clearance processes while meeting the Government's functional, clinical, operational, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and identity management requirements. The Government is particularly interested in determining whether industry currently offers solutions that satisfy these requirements through existing commercial capabilities, configurable platforms, or whether custom software development would be required. Specifically, the Government seeks information regarding industry's capability to provide solutions that: Support OSHA-compliant respirator medical questionnaire and evaluation clearance processes in accordance with OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard (29 CFR 1910.134). Provide automated questionnaire evaluation using configurable clinical decision logic to determine medical clearance or referral for further medical evaluation. Support physician review and follow-up medical evaluation processes performed by board-certified occupational medicine physicians. Provide secure electronic submission, storage, and review of follow-up medical documentation. Support user notification, medical clearance status tracking, reporting, and administrative case management. Support multiple federal customer agencies through configurable role-based administrative capabilities. Support SAML 2.0 or OpenID for integration with the Government's identity management environment. Implement phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication (MFA) for both internal government users and external customers in accordance with applicable federal cybersecurity requirements and guidance. Comply with applicable federal cybersecurity, privacy, records management, and Section 508 accessibility requirements. Support implementation within a federal environment requiring compliance with applicable HHS security requirements and an Authority to Operate (ATO), as applicable. The Government intends to use information obtained through this RFI to: Determine whether the Government's requirements can be satisfied through existing commercial capabilities, configurable commercial platforms, or custom-developed solutions. Assess the maturity of available commercial capabilities. Identify qualified vendors capable of satisfying the Government's requirements. Better understand implementation approaches, technical risks, and available commercial capabilities. Refine the Government's acquisition strategy and support development of any future solicitation. Anticipated Period of Performance The anticipated Period of Performance for this Solicitation is: Contract Period Period of Performance Base Period October 31, 2027 to October 30, 2028 Period 1 October 31, 2028 to October 30, 2029 Period 2 October 31, 2029 to October 30, 2030 Period 3 October 31, 2030 to October 30, 2031 Period 4 October 31, 2031 to October 30, 2032 Project Requirements The Government is seeking information regarding solutions capable of satisfying the functional, clinical, operational, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and identity management requirements described in the Government's accompanying requirements documentation. The desired solution should include, but is not limited to, the capability to: Provide a secure, web-based Respirator Medical Questionnaire and Evaluation Tool that supports OSHA respirator medical evaluation and clearance requirements. Utilize automated questionnaire evaluation and configurable clinical decision logic to identify individuals who may be medically cleared or referred for further medical evaluation. title: Human Hindbrain Organoid Functional Assay Services.
description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), Division of Applied Regulatory Science (DARS), intends to award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price purchase order to OrganoTherapeutics SARL for Human iPSC-Derived Hindbrain Organoid Functional Assay Services. The requirement includes the provision of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived hindbrain organoids and associated materials necessary to support in vitro research evaluating drug-induced effects on respiratory-relevant neural circuits. The contractor will also perform functional characterization of the organoids using three-dimensional multi-electrode array (3D MEA) technology to assess electrophysiological responses to drugs known to affect respiratory function. The functional characterization includes testing FDA-identified drug and reversal-agent combinations, MEA measurements, evaluation of batch-to-batch reproducibility, collection of exposed drug solutions for FDA verification, data analysis, and delivery of raw data, analyzed data, analysis files, and study reports. The requirement also includes twelve scheduled deliveries of human hindbrain organoids to the FDA White Oak Campus. The first delivery will consist of 96 organoids, with subsequent deliveries consisting of 48 organoids each. Functional characterization will be performed at the contractor's laboratory. The anticipated period of performance is eighteen (18) months from the date of award. This acquisition is being conducted as a commercial service acquisition under RFO FAR Part 12. The Government's decision to restrict competition is documented pursuant to RFO FAR 12.102(a). Market research identified OrganoTherapeutics SARL as the only source capable of satisfying the Government's complete requirement for both the required human hindbrain organoids and associated functional assay services. This notice is not intended to restrict consideration of any responsible source capable of meeting the Government's complete requirement. All responsible sources may submit a quotation and supporting capability information by the response date identified in this notice. Any timely response demonstrating the capability to satisfy the Government's complete requirement will be considered by the Contracting Officer prior to award.
